claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation. Let me start with a few basic ones:

1. How many children do you have that you're inquiring about for Child Benefit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you at home.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! And just to confirm - are you the person responsible for Alex? That is, do you provide for his day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and general care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for Alex - I take care of all his day-to-day needs like his food, clothes, and everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. One final question:

Does Alex have any special circumstances, such as:
- Being in hospital or residential care for extended periods?
- Living away from home for any reason?
- Working 24 hours or more per week?
- Receiving any benefits in his own right?

Or is he living with you full-time and attending school as a typical 8-year-old would?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - Alex has been in hospital for quite a while now, about three months or so. He's been receiving treatment there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that important information. I need to understand this situation a bit better as it may affect your Child Benefit eligibility.

You mentioned Alex has been in hospital for about three months. During this time, have you been regularly spending money on Alex - for example, on things like clothes, toys, treats, or other items for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have. I still buy things for him - clothes, his favorite snacks and treats, magazines to keep him entertained while he's in there. I make sure he has what he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good News!

**You ARE eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Even though Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you still qualify for Child Benefit because there is an important exception to the usual rule. When a child is in a UK hospital for over 12 weeks, you can continue to receive Child Benefit as long as you are regularly spending money on them - which you are doing by buying Alex clothes, snacks, treats, and magazines.

You meet all the standard eligibility criteria:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is under 16 years old (he's 8)
- You are responsible for his care and provide for his needs
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

Since you're continuing to regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital, you should be able to continue receiving Child Benefit. However, it's important that you inform HMRC about Alex's hospital stay if you haven't already done so, as they need to be aware of this situation to confirm the exception applies.

I hope Alex recovers well soon!

The claimant has confirmed they regularly spend money on Alex, buying him clothes, snacks, treats, and magazines while he's in hospital. This meets the exception criteria under the 'After 8 or 12 weeks' section of the rules. No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, and he is under 16 years old. Therefore, the claimant qualifies for Child Benefit for Alex.
